lustre-file-system.help:
A Lustre file system is a parallel file system that is used as a storage solution for HPC/AI/ML workloads. For more information, see [File Storage with Lustre].

To use any of the API operations, you must be authorized in an IAM policy. If you're not authorized, talk to an administrator. If you're an administrator who needs to write policies to give users access, see [Getting Started with Policies].

object-storage-link.help:
Object Storage links create the relationship between a directory in an File Storage with Lustre file system and a path within an Object Storage bucket. For more information, see [Syncing Lustre file systems with Object Storage].

To use any of the API operations, you must be authorized in an IAM policy. If you're not authorized, talk to an administrator. If you're an administrator who needs to write policies to give users access, see [Getting Started with Policies].

params.name: wait_for_state
params.help: This operation asynchronously creates, modifies or deletes a resource and uses a work request to track the progress of the operation. Specify this option to perform the action and then wait until the work request reaches a certain state. Multiple states can be specified, returning on the first state. For example, --wait-for-state ACCEPTED --wait-for-state CANCELED would return on whichever lifecycle state is reached first. If timeout is reached, a return code of 2 is returned. For any other error, a return code of 1 is returned.

params.name: wait_interval_seconds
params.help: Check every --wait-interval-seconds to see whether the work request has reached the state defined by --wait-for-state. Defaults to 30 seconds.

lustre-file-system create.help:
Creates a Lustre file system. 
[Command Reference](createLustreFileSystem)

params.name: compartment_id
params.help: The [OCID] of the compartment that contains the Lustre file system. [required]

params.name: availability_domain
params.help:
The availability domain the file system is in. May be unset as a blank or NULL value.

Example: `Uocm:PHX-AD-1` [required]

params.name: file_system_name
params.help: The Lustre file system name. This is used in mount commands and other aspects of the client command line interface. The file system name is limited to 8 characters. Allowed characters are lower and upper case English letters, numbers, and '_'. If you have multiple Lustre file systems mounted on the same clients, this name can help distinguish them. [required]

params.name: capacity_in_gbs
params.help: Capacity of the Lustre file system in GB. You can increase capacity only in multiples of 5 TB. [required]

params.name: subnet_id
params.help: The [OCID] of the subnet the Lustre file system is in. [required]

params.name: performance_tier
params.help: The Lustre file system performance tier. A value of `MBPS_PER_TB_125` represents 125 megabytes per second per terabyte. [required]

in a file, modifying it as needed and then passing it back in via the file:// syntax.
